prerequisites: Distinguish a valid model from a picture that violates a premise.
An explicit some-statement requires a witness; universal statements alone do not.
explanation: Possible means true in at least one valid model. Certain means true in every valid model. Every certain claim is also possible when the premises are consistent. The answer category possible but not certain is narrower: it requires one supporting model and one falsifying model. Impossible means false in every valid model. Check consistency first; no valid model means the premises are inconsistent, not a license to call any claim possible.

worked.action: Suppose all L are M. Can some M be L?
worked.justification: Yes: put one object in both L and M. This establishes possibility only.

worked.action: Keep all L are M but put one object only in M and leave L empty.
worked.justification: Now some M are L is false. The claim is possible but not certain because both models satisfy the premise.

worked.action: Suppose some L are M. The claim some M are L is certain.
worked.justification: The required overlap witness satisfies both expressions in every valid model. Certainty includes possibility.

worked.action: Suppose no L are M. The claim some L are M is impossible.
worked.justification: Any supporting witness would violate the premise; empty categories do not create an overlap.

worked.action: Suppose some L are M and no L are M simultaneously.
worked.justification: The first premise requires a witness in the region the second forbids. There is no valid model; check this before classifying a claim.

worked.action: All badges are tokens, and some tokens are red. Some badges being red is possible but not certain.
worked.justification: A red badge/token supports it. A red token with no badges falsifies it. Treat category names only as the stated sets, not as extra real-world facts.
